name: Concentration Curl
description: The concentration curl is a seated, single-arm curl performed with the elbow braced against the inner thigh, completely eliminating swinging and momentum. This isolation technique concentrates all the load directly on the biceps brachii, particularly the short head, and allows strong peak contraction at the top of the movement. It is one of the most effective exercises for isolating the biceps muscle.

execution.starting_position: Sit on the edge of a flat bench, feet flat on the floor, spread wider than hip-width. Hold a dumbbell in one hand and brace the back of the upper arm against the inner thigh on the same side. Arm is extended downward.
execution.setup_instructions: Sit with feet wide apart. Use a dumbbell light enough to perform with strict form. The key is brace the elbow against the inner thigh.
steps: Step 1: Sit on the bench, feet wide. Hold a dumbbell in one hand, upper arm pressed firmly against the inner thigh.
Step 2: Begin with the arm fully extended toward the floor, palm facing up.
Step 3: Exhale and curl the dumbbell upward by bending the elbow, keeping the upper arm stationary against the thigh.
Step 4: Curl until the forearm is roughly vertical; hold the peak contraction for 1 second, then inhale and lower slowly.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl up; inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow drift away from the thigh, which removes the isolation
Swinging the torso to assist the curl at the bottom
safety_considerations: Full extension at the bottom ensures maximum bicep stretch — do not limit ROM
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom to full curl at the top — the forearm stops near vertical.
coaching_cues: Pin the elbow to the inner thigh and do not let it move
Think about bringing your pinky to your shoulder at the top to maximize short head contraction
